candidates.name: Epididymo-orchitis
support_spans: Scrotal investigation revealed an enlarged testis, epididymis, and infected appendages.
Doppler ultrasonography: Revealed an enlarged left testis with heterogeneous echo pattern, enhanced vascularity, and retained testicular blood flow.
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings are consistent with epididymo-orchitis, an inflammation of the epididymis and testis.

candidates.name: Testicular torsion
support_spans: No torsion was evident in the sperm vessels;
contradict_spans: No torsion was evident in the sperm vessels;
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms could have suggested testicular torsion, but the absence of torsion in the sperm vessels rules out this diagnosis.

candidates.name: Hemorrhagic infarction
support_spans: Pathological examination: Showed hemorrhagic infarction of the left testicular appendage
candidates.why: The pathological examination confirms hemorrhagic infarction, which is a possible complication of epididymo-orchitis.

candidates.name: Testicular infarction
support_spans: MRI Image (at 60 days): Left testis showed no enhancement in T2, indicating disappearance of the left testis.
